classifiedFindings.label: PRICE-SCALE-MAGNITUDE-FOOTGUN
classifiedFindings.plausibility: n/a (no attacker path; owner deploy-time config hazard)
classifiedFindings.c4Category: QA/Low — State handling / configuration hazard (Law-3 non-obvious operational footgun)

classification.assetImpact: None to principal or third parties. priceScale never touches the budget ledger; every payout is bounded by the real funded balance via _safePay's shortfall-revert. No theft, no insolvency, no third-party value leak. The only effect is mis-sizing the emission RATE/runway: too-high collapses runway (budget/R) so earliest stakers over-earn until premature depletion and emissions pause until a top-up; too-low floor-divides newRate toward zero, silently re-introducing the floor-to-zero degradation the contract exists to fix.
attackPath: No attacker. Trigger is a deploy-time owner choice of the immutable priceScale.
1. Owner deploys NFTStakerPriceScaled with priceScale != 10**(rewardDecimals - priceDecimals).
2. Constructor only checks _priceScale != 0 (L230); no upper bound, no decimal-consistency check.
3. _recomputeSchedule multiplies latestPrice * priceScale (L435), silently mis-sizing the rate.

4. Effect manifests over time as collapsed runway / premature depletion (too-high) or floor-to-zero emission (too-low). No revert until an absurd overflow-scale (the obvious-misconfig leg, out of scope).
classification.likelihood: Low — requires the trusted owner to supply a wrong-magnitude immutable that is plausible (off-by-decimals) yet non-obvious, with no on-deploy signal.
classification.assumptions: Owner is non-malicious (Law-3). The wrong value is a plausible off-by-decimals magnitude, not an absurd overflow value (that leg reverts and is the suppressed obvious-misconfig PS-004).
classification.externalRequirements: None. No external/attacker action is involved; self-correctable by the owner via setTargetAPY (priceScale and targetAPY are independent linear factors on the rate).

severityRationale.notHigh: No direct asset theft/loss via any valid attack path. priceScale is solvency-insensitive; payouts are bounded by the funded balance through _safePay's shortfall-revert. No attacker can reach this; no funds are stolen or lost.
severityRationale.notMedium: No protocol-availability impact via external/attacker action and no value-leak-with-stated-assumptions caused by anyone other than the trusted owner's own deploy-time config choice. Both legs are owner-recoverable (runway re-sizing or rate correction via setTargetAPY); there is no external requirement and no third-party loss.
severityRationale.isLow: State-handling / configuration hazard: an unchecked immutable silently mis-sizes the emission rate/runway with a non-obvious, surprising consequence. Per Law 3 this is an in-scope operational footgun (a competent non-malicious owner would be surprised that the magnitude the feature exists to normalize is itself unverifiable), distinct from the obvious-misconfig overflow leg that was correctly suppressed in dedup. Correctly capped at Low.

classifiedFindings.justification: Confirms the provisional Low. The immutable priceScale has no upper bound and no decimal-consistency check, so the contract structurally cannot verify priceScale == 10**(rewardDecimals - priceDecimals). A wrong magnitude silently mis-sizes the emission rate/runway, but solvency is structurally insensitive and the trusted owner self-corrects via setTargetAPY. Not High (no theft/loss path, budget-bounded), not Medium (no external/attacker availability impact or third-party value leak; owner-recoverable). Valid Low operational footgun, in scope under Law-3 as a non-obvious deploy-time config hazard.
classifiedFindings.qaOneLiner: L: NFTStakerPriceScaled's immutable priceScale is unbounded and decimal-unchecked (constructor only guards != 0), so a wrong-magnitude deploy value silently mis-sizes the emission rate/runway (too-high collapses runway → premature depletion; too-low re-introduces floor-to-zero) — solvency-safe and owner-correctable via setTargetAPY, but recommend a deploy-time assert that priceScale == 10**(rewardDecimals - priceDecimals).
classifiedFindings.remediation: Add a deploy-time invariant tying priceScale to the actual decimal regime, e.g. require(priceScale == 10 ** (rewardToken.decimals() - priceTokenDecimals)) in the constructor, or pass priceTokenDecimals and derive priceScale internally so the magnitude cannot be supplied inconsistently. At minimum, document the exact expected magnitude per dispatcher price-token decimal regime and bound priceScale to prevent silent over-sizing.
